newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps flat to weaker in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps flat to weaker in thin trading.

text.p: European oil swaps were on Monday seen mainly flat or slightly weaker on lower screen values on a day that saw little open trading activity.
Heavy fuel swaps eased 50 cents a tonne but trading was thin.
September barges traded at $93.50 and October between $94.50 and $95 but traders said the slow physical market was hampering activity.
Low sulphur stayed well bid after edging slightly up against barges last week.
"We're still well bid on the high-lows," said a broker.
High sulphur cargoes continued to be sharply discounted to barges, trading at $3 a tonne below for September.
In recent years cargoes have typically traded around $1 a tonne above barges.
But a lack of cargo demand has eroded that premium and dealers see little cargo buying from power companies in the short-term.
Brent CFDs slipped a cent or two with lower outright values and remained in shallow contango.
This week talked 32 cents under October with the following three weeks at 29 cents, 27 cents and 24 cents under respectively.

Brokers could see no change in bid-offer quotes for gas oil cracks against Brent or for gas oil differentials, although jet values did appear to fall $0.25, certainly for October and the fourth quarter.
The October jet differentials decline to either side of $21.50, at which level a solitary deal was heard done.
Gasoline swaps showed most change, declining $2.50 on the day to $196.50-$198 on the back of a $1-$2 weakening on prompt barges and significant NYMEX losses.

A private and confidential September swap deal was rumoured earlier done equivalent to around $4.90 on a crack basis. Brokers later placed crack talk in the $4.80-$4.90 range, well done from morning ideas in the $4.85-$5.05 range.
The December crack was heard offered at $3.15, first quarter 1998 around $3, the second around $3.45, and the third and fourth around $4.70 and $2.50 respectively.

Naphtha was talked $2 lower at $184.50-$185.25 for September, with values all the way back to December seen virtually flat to the September quote on a day when dealers expected physical quotes also to fall by around $2.
